stories.source_title: Nigeria adds second-highest airline seats in Africa in September, reaches 1.19 million
stories.source_excerpt: Nigeria added 322,800 scheduled airline seats in September 2026, taking its total capacity to 1.19 million seats and giving it the second-highest increase among Africa’s top 10 aviation markets, according to OAG African Market data. The post Nigeria adds second-highest airline seats in Africa in September, reaches 1.19 million appeared first on Nairametrics .
stories.headline: Nigeria Boosts Aviation Capacity With Massive Seat Expansion in September
stories.dek: Fresh data shows the nation pulling off the second-highest increase in scheduled airline seats across the African continent.
stories.body: Nigeria's aviation sector has recorded a notable expansion in capacity as it heads deeper into the month. According to OAG African Market data highlighted by Nairametrics, the country successfully introduced 322,800 scheduled airline seats specifically for September 2026. This substantial addition pushes the nation's overall aviation capacity up to an impressive 1.19 million seats. The development marks a significant milestone for the local market, placing Nigeria securely at the forefront of growth. Among the top ten aviation markets operating across the African continent, this expansion represents the second-highest increase recorded for the period. Industry observers note that such growth reflects shifting dynamics in travel demand and route planning. As carriers adjust their schedules to accommodate more passengers, the rising availability of seats is expected to influence connectivity and overall market activity throughout the region as the busy travel season progresses.

stories.dek: The Cameroon Football Federation president is throwing his weight behind the FIFA boss amid mounting controversy over tournament stake sales.
stories.body: Cameroon Football Federation president Samuel Eto'o has stepped forward to advocate for leadership stability within global football administration. Information published by Africanews reveals that Eto'o is encouraging continental football chiefs to throw their backing behind FIFA president Gianni Infantino. This show of support arrives at a challenging juncture for the governing body's leadership. Infantino has recently found himself facing considerable pressure and pushback from various quarters regarding a controversial proposal. The plan in question involves attempting to sell stakes in the prestigious World Cup tournament. As the backlash over the proposed sell-off continues to unfold, key figures within African football are being called upon to pick a side. By urging solidarity with the current FIFA administration, Eto'o highlights the ongoing political alignments and power dynamics shaping the future governance of international football as stakeholders debate the commercialization of the sport's biggest global showcase.

stories.headline: Nigerian Government Pushes Manufacturers to Utilize ECOWAS Trade Scheme
stories.dek: Authorities are intensifying efforts to boost regional exports and deepen West African economic integration.
stories.body:
The Federal Government is urging local manufacturers and business owners to tap into the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme (ETLS) to scale up their export operations. Details provided by Nairametrics reveal that the initiative is designed to help Nigerian products reach wider markets across the West African region.

By maximizing the benefits of the ETLS, regional trade integration is expected to deepen significantly. Officials believe that easing cross-border trade barriers will empower domestic producers to increase their international footprint.

The push comes as part of broader governmental efforts to strengthen the economy through non-oil exports and regional cooperation. Manufacturers are being encouraged to familiarize themselves with the framework to unlock new commercial avenues.

As these promotional efforts ramp up, stakeholders hope to see a tangible rise in intra-African trade volumes. The strategy aims to position Nigerian enterprises for greater competitiveness within the wider ECOWAS market.

stories.source_title: UN General Assembly adopts new world map that shows Africa's true size
stories.source_excerpt: The United Nations General Assembly on Friday endorsed a new world map that reflects Africa's size more accurately. The resolution, sponsored by Togo, was passed with 164 member states voting in favour. The US voted against.
stories.headline: UN General Assembly Adopts New Map Highlighting Africa's True Scale
stories.dek: A Togo-sponsored resolution successfully passes with overwhelming support from member states to correct continental cartography.
stories.body:
The United Nations General Assembly has officially endorsed a revised world map that offers a more accurate representation of Africa's actual geographic size. Africanews reports that the resolution, which was put forward by Togo, gained widespread approval during Friday's session.

A total of 164 member states cast their votes in favor of the adoption, reflecting a broad international consensus on updating the traditional cartographic standards. However, the United States stood out by voting against the measure.

For decades, critics have argued that standard world maps disproportionately shrink the African continent due to projection distortions. The newly adopted map seeks to rectify these longstanding visual inaccuracies.

This diplomatic milestone marks a significant moment for international representation and geographical awareness at the global body. The decision is expected to influence educational materials and official representations moving forward.

stories.source_title: Xenophobia Can’t Break Africa’s Most Fruitful Musical Partnership

stories.headline: Music Bridges the Gap Between Nigeria and South Africa
stories.dek: Despite political tensions and xenophobic hurdles, the enduring creative bond between Nigeria and South Africa continues to thrive.
stories.body:
When political landscapes shift and diplomatic friction arises, nations often find themselves drifting apart. Yet, as reported by The NATIVE, music has consistently acted as a stubborn, unifying force between Nigeria and South Africa. Even when external factors attempt to create distance, artists and fans across both regions refuse to let the connection sever.

This cross-border collaboration remains one of the continent's most fruitful artistic partnerships. Time and again, sounds flow effortlessly from Lagos to Johannesburg and back, proving that cultural affinity runs far deeper than political discourse. Creators continue to lean into this shared sonic space, producing tracks that capture the imagination of millions.

Ultimately, the creative synergy between these two African powerhouses defies attempts at division. As artists continue to prioritize collaboration, the music scene shows that shared rhythms and melodies can transcend political boundaries and keep communities anchored together.

For followers of the continent's creative evolution, this enduring bond is a testament to the resilience of African art. No matter the friction in other sectors, the musical bridge linking Nigeria and South Africa remains open, vibrant, and entirely unbreakable.

stories.source_title: Why Nigerian startups are turning to debt over equity
stories.source_excerpt: Debt now accounts for a record 41% of all capital raised by African tech startups, up from just 17% in 2019, according to Partech Africa's annual venture capital report. The post Why Nigerian startups are turning to debt over equity appeared first on Nairametrics .
stories.headline: Nigerian Startups Pivot From Equity to Debt Financing
stories.dek: Partech Africa's annual venture capital report reveals that debt has surged to account for 41 percent of capital raised by African tech startups.
stories.body:
The funding landscape for African tech innovators is undergoing a profound transformation. According to findings from Partech Africa's annual venture capital report, debt has risen sharply to claim a record 41 percent of all capital secured by startups on the continent.

This represents a massive shift from historical funding patterns, particularly when compared to 2019, when debt accounted for a mere 17 percent of total capital raised. As traditional equity rounds become more complex or cautious, founders across Nigeria and the wider region are increasingly exploring alternative financing avenues.

Turning to debt allows growing ventures to secure necessary capital without diluting founder ownership or giving away substantial equity too early in their life cycles. This strategic pivot reflects a maturing ecosystem where businesses are learning to navigate different financial instruments to fuel their expansion.

While equity still plays a vital role, the growing reliance on debt highlights a more pragmatic, resilient approach to startup financing. As ecosystem participants adapt to changing economic realities, debt financing is firmly cementing its place as a cornerstone of African tech growth.
